mcqs.q: Whole-genome analysis of the FCV strains causing paw and mouth disease in this household showed they were:
o: Genetically distinct from prior paw-and-mouth and virulent systemic disease FCVs
mcqs.e: Sequencing showed the strains were genetically diverse from previously reported paw-and-mouth and VSD-associated FCVs.

mcqs.q: What was the status of the second cat sharing the household?
mcqs.e: A cohabiting cat was infected with FCV yet remained asymptomatic.

mcqs.q: The phenotype of these isolates differed from respiratory FCVs in that they were:
mcqs.e: The isolates were resistant to low pH, only slightly susceptible to bile salts, but susceptible to trypsin—a pattern unlike respiratory FCVs.

mcqs.q: The liposome-dual TLR3/9 agonist nanoparticle eye drops acted against FHV-1 primarily by:
o: Inducing type I and II interferon responses
mcqs.e: The nanoparticles induced both type I and II interferon responses and suppressed FHV-1 replication.

mcqs.q: In the recrudescent FHV-1 cat model, twice-daily nanoparticle treatment resulted in:
o: Significantly fewer episodes of viral shedding
mcqs.e: Treated cats had lessened ocular signs and significantly fewer viral shedding episodes than controls.

mcqs.q: The authors concluded ocular immunotherapy is:
o: A promising novel approach for HSV-1/FHV-1 ocular infection
mcqs.e: They concluded non-specific ocular immunotherapy offers significant promise for treating HSV-1 and FHV-1 ocular infections.

mcqs.q: Which pathogen was most frequently detected among FRDC-suspected cats by the new multiplex assays?
mcqs.e: Mycoplasma felis (61.9%) was the most commonly detected pathogen.

mcqs.q: Co-infection was detected in what proportion of the clinical specimens?
mcqs.e: Co-infection was present in 57.1% of samples, with 92.1% positive for at least one pathogen.

mcqs.q: SARS-CoV-2 in this feline cohort was:
o: Found in the majority of cats
mcqs.e: SARS-CoV-2 was detected in just two specimens, indicating it was rare.

mcqs.q: Compared with doxycycline alone, adding famciclovir in kittens with mild ocular IURD resulted in:
o: Faster clinical recovery and fewer corneal disease cases
mcqs.e: Group DF (famciclovir) recovered faster and significantly fewer developed corneal disease than group D.

mcqs.q: All five kittens removed from the study for worsening signs belonged to:
mcqs.e: All five kittens whose signs worsened enough to be withdrawn were in group D (placebo).

mcqs.q: For shelters, the authors suggested early famciclovir in mild cases may:
o: Reduce length of stay and time to adoption
mcqs.e: They concluded famciclovir may reduce corneal disease, length of stay, and time to adoption, increasing capacity for care.

mcqs.q: Detection of Mycoplasma felis in feline BALF was significantly associated with:
o: Radiographic alveolar lesions and BALF neutrophilia
mcqs.e: M felis positivity was associated with radiographic alveolar lesions and increased BALF neutrophils.

mcqs.q: How did M felis detection affect prognosis (risk of death)?
o: No significant difference in risk of death
mcqs.e: There was no significant difference in risk of death between M+ and M- cats.

mcqs.q: Eosinophil percentage in BALF was:
mcqs.e: Eosinophils were higher in the M- group (25%) than in the M+ group (9%).

mcqs.q: Across 4616 canine and feline respiratory samples in early 2020, SARS-CoV-2 was:
mcqs.e: No SARS-CoV-2 infections were identified among the samples.

mcqs.q: The study concluded that respiratory disease in these tested pets was caused by:
mcqs.e: Disease was attributed to common veterinary pathogens, with SARS-CoV-2 infection rare in pets.

mcqs.q: Comparing the February–April periods of 2019 and 2020, positive respiratory results were:
mcqs.e: Positive respiratory results were similar between the two years.

mcqs.q: Overall, this scoping review concluded that cats play what role in spreading SARS-CoV-2?
mcqs.e: Cats appeared to play a limited role in SARS-CoV-2 spread.

mcqs.q: Regarding circulation of SARS-CoV-2 among cats under natural conditions, the review found:
o: No current evidence of circulation among cats
Cats are not susceptible at all
mcqs.e: Despite susceptibility and reverse zoonosis from humans, there was no evidence of SARS-CoV-2 circulating among cats.

mcqs.q: A key research gap identified was:
o: Underrepresentation of stray, feral, and shelter cat populations
mcqs.e: Gaps included a lack of large-scale studies and underrepresentation of stray, feral, and shelter cats.

mcqs.q: Dogs' limited susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 is attributed mainly to:
o: Low respiratory ACE2 levels and phylogenetic distance of canine ACE2
mcqs.e: Low ACE2 in the respiratory tract plus phylogenetic distance of canine ACE2 reduce spike binding affinity.

mcqs.q: The review highlighted detection dogs as a method to:
o: Discriminate SARS-CoV-2 infected from non-infected individuals
Replace PCR for animal diagnosis only
mcqs.e: Detection dogs reliably distinguished infected from non-infected people using secretions, saliva, and sweat.

mcqs.q: The risk of SARS-CoV-2 transmission by domestic dogs was characterized as:
mcqs.e: Transmission by dogs is uncommon, though it remains a concern warranting preventive measures.

mcqs.q: Beagles experimentally inoculated with SARS-CoV-2 or MERS-CoV shed virus in:
mcqs.e: The dogs shed virus in nasal secretions, feces, and urine.

mcqs.q: Clinical signs observed in the inoculated dogs included:
o: Weight loss and increased body temperature
mcqs.e: The dogs showed weight loss and increased body temperature.

mcqs.q: A SARS-CoV-2 clinical characteristic identified in the dogs was:
mcqs.e: Increased LDH levels, characteristic of SARS-CoV-2, were identified along with lung pathology.

mcqs.q: Among the 1018 pets tested in Korea, SARS-CoV-2 viral RNA was detected in:
mcqs.e: Viral RNA was found in only 2 of 1018 pets, both cats.

mcqs.q: Antigens and/or antibodies to SARS-CoV-2 were detected:
o: Only in pets of confirmed COVID-19 households
Even in animal shelters and regardless of household infection status
mcqs.e: Markers were found regardless of whether the household was infected, including in shelter animals previously considered safe.

mcqs.q: ELISA seropositivity was higher in:
mcqs.e: Cats had higher seropositivity (5.20%) than dogs (2.38%) by ELISA.

mcqs.q: Among pets identified through passive surveillance, what proportion had reported exposure to a person with COVID-19 before infection?
mcqs.e: 94% of passively detected pets had prior exposure to a person with COVID-19.

mcqs.q: Clinical signs of illness were present in:
o: 74% of passively-detected vs 27% of actively-detected pets
mcqs.e: Signs were present in 74% of passively-surveilled pets but only 27% of those found by active surveillance.

mcqs.q: The study's main conclusion about how pets become infected was:
o: Primarily following exposure to an infected person, often their owner
mcqs.e: Cats and dogs primarily became infected after exposure to a person with COVID-19, most often their owners.

mcqs.q: What was identified as a risk factor for SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity in these dogs?
o: Adult (older) age, ~4.16x odds vs young dogs
mcqs.e: Seropositivity was age-related, with adult dogs about 4.16 times more likely to be positive than young dogs.

mcqs.q: RT-qPCR testing of the 111 dogs (222 swabs) showed:
mcqs.e: All oropharyngeal and rectal swabs tested negative by RT-qPCR.

mcqs.q: The detected IgG antibodies were directed against the:
o: Nucleocapsid (N) protein, with none reacting to Spike
mcqs.e: 20.22% had IgG against the N protein, while none reacted to the Spike protein.
